calls.summary: Priya Nair, VP of CX at a retail eCommerce brand, called to explore omnichannel voice and chat outsourcing paired with agentic AI. The agent mapped her volumes to a white-glove premium tier and scheduled a scoping consultation with sales. Priya confirmed the date and asked for a case study to be emailed.

Marcus Feldman, an ML lead at a computer-vision startup, called about AI data labeling and annotation for model training. The agent explained dataset curation timelines and per-project pricing, then booked a technical consultation. Marcus was pleased and shared his data volumes on the call.

Elena Ross, an operations manager, called for a status update on her Learning as a Service onboarding curriculum program. The agent confirmed the current design milestone and pulled up the delivery schedule. Elena was satisfied with the progress and did not need anything further.

Daniel Okafor, founder of a fintech startup, called to schedule a consultation about outsourcing his customer support team. The agent collected his company name, seat count, and target channels, then set up a new discovery consultation with the sales team. Daniel was clear on next steps before hanging up.

Sophia Lindqvist, a trust and safety director at a social platform, called about content moderation and policy enforcement coverage. The agent outlined moderator staffing and wellness support, then scheduled a consultation to scope the queue volumes. Sophia appreciated the clinical wellness component.

Raj Patel from procurement called about an invoice discrepancy on his monthly per-FTE billing. The agent reviewed the account and flagged the line item for the finance team to correct. Raj wanted a follow-up email confirming the adjustment.

Hannah Cole, an AI researcher, called for status on her RLHF response scoring and data labeling deliverables. The agent checked the project tracker and gave an updated completion window. Hannah noted the turnaround was slower than expected.

Tomas Rivera, head of support at a mobility app, called to explore agentic AI deployment with human-in-the-loop escalation. The agent explained the AI agent design workflow and scheduled a consultation with a solutions architect. Tomas asked several pricing questions before agreeing.

Grace Kim, a compliance officer at a regional bank, called about outsourcing AML and KYC transaction monitoring. The agent described the analyst staffing model and regulatory coverage, then booked a consultation. Grace flagged a tight audit deadline that made her hesitant.

Victor Ambrose, an L and D manager, called frustrated about delays in an onboarding training rollout for his agents. The agent apologized and escalated the program timeline to the delivery lead. Victor wanted assurance the launch would not slip again.

Nadia Farouk, a program lead, called to complain about SLA misses and gaps in her compliance reporting. The agent logged the issues and promised a review from the account manager. Nadia remained unhappy with the lack of a firm resolution date.

Owen Bradley, a product manager, called to cancel a pilot engagement for AI red-teaming due to a budget freeze. The agent confirmed the cancellation terms and noted the account for potential re-engagement. Owen declined an offer to pause instead of cancel.

An inbound caller left a voicemail about a content moderation vendor RFP with a short deadline. No agent was available and the call rolled to voicemail. The message requested a same-day callback from sales.

Carla Mendez called with a billing dispute over an overage on data labeling hours she said were never approved. The agent could not locate the change order and routed the case to finance. Carla was irritated by the wait and asked to speak to a manager.

Isaac Trent called angry about the quality of recent content moderation output on his platform. The agent tried to gather examples but Isaac talked over the questions. The call ended without a resolution and an escalation ticket was opened.

transcript.text: Hi Marcus, I found your number on your website. I run customer support operations for an e-commerce company based in Austin, and we're really stretched thin. We need help scaling.

transcript.text: Great, I'm glad you reached out. We work with retailers and e-commerce brands every day. Can I get your first and last name for my notes?

transcript.text: Both, honestly. We have voice, chat, and email tickets piling up. We want humans, but we also want your AI tools to route smarter. You know, like agentic AI helping us move faster.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Absolutely, that's our sweet spot. Our CX team combines omnichannel support with AI augmentation to handle scale without losing the human touch. What ZIP code or city should I be thinking about for your operations?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: We're in Austin, Texas, 78704.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Excellent. Austin is part of our North America footprint. And just so I have this right, Jennifer Salazar, Austin. What's the best phone number to reach you at?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Sure, it's ****. You can also text that number.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Got it, ****. Just one more thing, what's your email address for follow-up materials?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Oh, um, I'll give you that when we actually book the call. I get a lot of spam.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I understand. So Jennifer, what I'd like to do is get you scheduled with one of our solutions consultants. Would next Thursday, October 31st at 10 AM work for an initial discovery call? That's about an hour.

transcript.speaker: caller

callDetail.aiSummary: Marcus Bell conducted an inbound lead qualification call with Jennifer Salazar, an e-commerce operations manager in Austin, Texas seeking omnichannel customer support and AI-augmented CX services. Marcus successfully captured the caller's name, ZIP code, phone number, and service interests, and scheduled a discovery consultation for October 31st at 10 AM. The caller did not provide an email address at intake, citing spam concerns, which represents a minor compliance gap. Overall, the call achieved its intake objectives and qualified the lead for consultative follow-up.

comment.author: Kyle Paklaian
comment.text: @Marcus, strong structure on this one. You nailed the greeting, the qualification questions, and the close. The Austin ZIP code and 10 AM slot are locked in. One coaching point: next time, emphasize why we need the email for the calendar invite and onboarding materials. That small push can unlock data and improve our follow-up rate. Also consider asking Jennifer how many support agents she currently has, so we can size the proposal. Great work overall.

transcript.text: Hi Marcus. My name is Priya Desai, I run trust operations at a social platform and we're looking for a content moderation partner. This is the first time we've reached out to you.

transcript.text: Great to meet you Priya, and thanks for thinking of us. So I understand your platform's needs, can you tell me roughly the volume you're moderating and which content types?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Sure. We're seeing a big spike in user generated video and we need policy enforcement plus some platform integrity work. We're a growing team, maybe fifteen to twenty moderators to start.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Understood. Our Trust and Safety service is a strong fit there. We staff specialized moderators, handle policy enforcement and escalations, and we pair it with our Wellness and Resiliency program to protect your teammates doing that difficult work.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: The wellness piece matters to us, honestly. But before we go further, what does something like that run per moderator? I want to keep this manageable while we scale.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's fair. Moderation typically lands between twenty eight hundred and five thousand per moderator each month depending on language coverage and complexity, and wellness is a small add-on on top. We can scope a tier that matches your starting volume so you're not overpaying early.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Okay. I'll be honest, we're also getting a quote from one of the bigger providers we already talked to, so I'm comparing a couple of options here.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That makes sense, and I'd encourage you to compare. Where we tend to stand out is the clinical rigor behind our wellness support and how fast we ramp specialized teams. I'm happy to put those specifics side by side for you.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: That would help. One more thing, I don't want to get locked into some huge long term commitment before we know it works for us.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Completely understand. We can start with a scoped pilot so you can validate quality before expanding. No need to commit to full scale up front.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: That's reassuring. What would the next step look like?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I'd like to book you a consultation with one of our Trust and Safety solution leads. They'll walk through volume, language coverage, the wellness program, and pilot pricing. Does Thursday at 10 AM work?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Thursday at 10 works. Let me just flag I may need to loop in our VP before we sign anything.
highlights: may need to loop in our VP

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: No problem at all, they're welcome to join. What's the best email to send the invite and a short prep summary to?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: It's priya.desai at the company domain, I'll watch for it.

transcript.speaker: agent

qaPairs.question: What services does TaskUs offer?
qaPairs.answer: We deliver Customer Experience, Agentic AI, Trust and Safety, AI data and operations, and specialized services like Sales and Learning as a Service. A short consultation with a specialist is the best way to map the right mix to your goals, and I can set that up.

qaPairs.question: How much does it cost to outsource customer support with TaskUs?
qaPairs.answer: Pricing is custom-scoped and typically billed per agent per month based on channels, languages, and volume. I can arrange a consultation where a specialist gives you an exact quote for your program.

qaPairs.question: Do you provide content moderation and trust and safety services?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we offer content moderation, policy enforcement, platform integrity, and CSAM response backed by clinical wellness support for our teams. Let's book a consultation to scope your specific policy needs.

qaPairs.question: Can TaskUs help us build and deploy AI agents?
qaPairs.answer: Absolutely, our Agentic AI teams handle AI agent design, deployment, human-in-the-loop escalation, and workflow automation. A specialist can walk you through an approach on a quick call, and I can schedule it.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer AI data labeling and annotation?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we provide data collection, labeling, annotation, and dataset curation for model training. I can set up a consultation to review your dataset volume and requirements.

qaPairs.question: What is RLHF and do you support it?
qaPairs.answer: We support RLHF, prompt and response scoring, and output evaluation to help align and validate models. Let's book a consultation so a specialist can detail the workflow for your team.

qaPairs.question: Do you handle AML and KYC compliance work?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our Financial Crime and Compliance teams cover KYC, AML, transaction monitoring, and fraud investigation. I can arrange a consultation to align on your regulatory scope.

qaPairs.question: How many languages and countries do you support?
qaPairs.answer: We operate across 14 countries and support more than 30 languages. A specialist can confirm coverage for your specific markets on a scoping call, and I can book it.

qaPairs.question: Can you scale a team quickly for a product launch or seasonal peak?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we ramp and flex staffing for launches and peak periods with proper lead time. Let's schedule a consultation to plan the timeline and headcount.

qaPairs.question: What industries do you work with?
qaPairs.answer: We serve Entertainment and Gaming, Financial Services, Healthcare, Mobility and Travel, Retail and eCommerce, Social Media, and Technology. A specialist can share relevant results for your industry on a call I can set up.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer red teaming and AI safety testing?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we run adversarial red-teaming, model blind-spot testing, and misuse prevention across modalities. I can book a consultation to review your model and scope.

qaPairs.question: How is TaskUs different from Concentrix or Teleperformance?
qaPairs.answer: We pair specialized talent with intelligent automation in a human-plus-AI model focused on measurable outcomes and wellness for our teams. A specialist can walk through a tailored comparison, and I can schedule that call.

qaPairs.question: Do you support autonomous vehicle programs?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we handle AV data annotation, sensor labeling, edge-case operations, and safety validation. Let's book a consultation to scope your program.

qaPairs.question: Can you provide sales outsourcing?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our Sales as a Service teams cover lead generation, SDR and BDR outsourcing, and pipeline management. I can arrange a consultation to review your revenue goals.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer training and onboarding programs?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our Learning as a Service builds onboarding curriculum, agent training, and knowledge management. A specialist can scope a program on a call I can set up.

qaPairs.question: How do you protect the wellbeing of moderators?
qaPairs.answer: We provide science-backed clinical wellness, psychological support, and resilience programs as an add-on to high-stakes work. Let's book a consultation to include this in your program design.

qaPairs.question: How long does it take to get started?
qaPairs.answer: Timelines depend on scope, staffing, and channels, and a specialist can give you a realistic launch plan. I can schedule a consultation to map your timeline.

qaPairs.question: Can I get a custom quote for my program?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, quotes are tailored to your service mix, headcount, and volume. Share a few details and I can book a consultation where a specialist provides an exact quote.

qaPairs.question: Do you work with NVIDIA, AWS, or Zendesk?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we co-market and integrate with partners including NVIDIA, AWS, Zendesk, Kustomer, and Decagon. A specialist can explain how those fit your stack on a call I can schedule.

qaPairs.question: How do I speak with someone about starting a program?
qaPairs.answer: The fastest path is a consultation with a TaskUs solutions specialist who can scope and quote your needs. Share your service interest and region and I will set up the appointment.
